evidence.heading: Frequently Asked Questions › Ordering › How do I place an order?
evidence.content:
Three ways, all against the same menu and account:

1. **Website** — browse the menu, add to cart, and check out.

   coffee"); the assistant builds an order draft you confirm before anything

evidence.heading: Frequently Asked Questions › Ordering › What are your hours?
evidence.content:
Kitchen hours are set by the restaurant and shown on the site. Outside
hours, or when the kitchen is temporarily paused, checkout is disabled and
the assistant will say so rather than take an order it can't fulfil.

evidence.heading: Ordering, Cancellation & Refund Policies › Cancellation policy
evidence.content:
- You may cancel an order yourself **only while it is in PLACED status** —
  i.e. before the kitchen confirms it. Use the order page or ask support.
- Once an order is CONFIRMED or COOKING, self-service cancellation is no
  longer possible (ingredients are committed). Contact support; staff can
  cancel at their discretion before the order is READY.
- Orders that are READY, OUT FOR DELIVERY, or DELIVERED cannot be cancelled.

evidence.heading: Ordering, Cancellation & Refund Policies › Hours & kitchen availability
evidence.content:
- Orders are accepted only within the kitchen's configured business hours;
  the restaurant may also pause the kitchen temporarily (rush, maintenance).
  While closed or paused, no channel — web, Telegram, or AI assistant — will
  accept an order.
- Individual dishes may have their own serving windows (e.g. breakfast-only
  items) and may sell out during the day.

evidence.heading: Frequently Asked Questions › Ordering › Can I customise a dish?
evidence.content:
Spice level can be adjusted on most cooked-to-order dishes (dosas, curries,
biryanis) — mention it in the item notes. Common requests: "less spicy",
"no onion", "chutney/masala packed separately", "ghee on the side".

evidence.content: Beverages serve all day, every day — no serving window.

evidence.heading: Rice, Pongal & Biryani Guide › Biryani
evidence.content:
Tamil-style biryani — Dindigul tradition: small-grain seeraga samba rice,
curd-marinated meat, and Chettinad masala. Distinct from Hyderabadi
biryani: smaller grain, deeper pepper notes, no saffron. All biryanis are
medium-hot and come with onion raita. Prep time 25–35 minutes — the longest
on the menu; on weekends demand spikes, so expect the upper end. All
biryanis serve 11:30 AM–10 PM IST (lunch and dinner).

The traditional cooler alongside biryani or Chettinad curries. Available
all day.
